keys.read_through: in order: sos.nh.gov (the New Hampshire Secretary of State's results workbooks), thegreenpapers.com/P28/ (pledged delegates, the conventions' roll calls, the New Hampshire vote as certified) and the Wikipedia API (primaries.py)
keys.earliest_call: when one good source carries the result and the nominee is known; provisional while the nominee is presumptive, the result is not certified, or Wikipedia is the only source
keys.revisions: An election result, a primary result and a fact do not change. A mistake in what was entered is corrected in the open: the first entry stays in the record.
keys.called_yes: The other party's nominee in its New Hampshire primary is not the winner.
keys.called_no: The same statement is false.
keys.stays_open: The primary has not been held, the nominee is not known, the evidence is not all in, no source could be read, or two sources contradict each other. Each is reported apart; none is a no. A source that has not been updated yet is a delay and holds nothing.
keys.checked: every Monday until 2028, then on the first run of every day
keys.checks: the highest source that has the figure is used; the others must not give the key a different answer (another winner, another nominee, a delegate count of the same kind on the other side of two-thirds). The state's workbooks must add up, county by county
keys.if_missing: The key stays open and keeps its chance. After July 15, 2028 it is held and the run is flagged every day.
keys.fallback: an entry by hand with its source, compared with what the sources give; if the two disagree the key is held
